# Esther Chapter 2 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 456v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/EST_002_page_001.jpg

---

**2:1** Some time later, after King Ahasuerus's fury had cooled, he began to think about Vashti — about what she had done and about the irreversible decree issued against her.

**2:2** His personal attendants suggested, "Why not search for beautiful young women for the king?

**2:3** Appoint officials in every province to bring all the most beautiful young virgins to the citadel in Susa. Place them in the women's quarters under Hegai, the royal eunuch in charge of the women, and give them the finest beauty treatments."

**2:4** "Then whichever young woman the king finds most pleasing can become queen in Vashti's place." The king liked this idea and put it into action.

**2:5** Now living in the citadel of Susa was a Jewish man named Mordecai — son of Jair, son of Shimei, son of Kish — from the tribe of Benjamin.

**2:6** His family had been taken from Jerusalem as part of the exile carried off with King Jeconiah of Judah by Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon.

**2:7** Mordecai had raised his cousin Hadassah — also known as Esther — because she had lost both her parents. She was a strikingly beautiful young woman, and when her father and mother died, Mordecai had adopted her as his own daughter.

**2:8** When the king's decree was announced and young women from across the empire were being brought to Susa, Esther was among those taken to the royal palace and placed in Hegai's care.

**2:9** Hegai was immediately impressed by her. She won his favor, and he gave her priority treatment — the best beauty regimen, the finest food, seven personally chosen attendants from the palace — and moved her into the most desirable rooms in the women's quarters.

**2:10** Esther kept her Jewish identity and family background a secret, exactly as Mordecai had told her to do.

**2:11** Every single day, Mordecai made his way to the courtyard near the women's quarters to find out how Esther was doing and what was happening to her.

**2:12** Before any young woman could go to the king, she had to complete a full year of beauty treatments — six months with oil of myrrh and six months with perfumes and other cosmetics. That was the required preparation.

**2:13** When her turn came, she could take anything she wanted with her from the women's quarters to the king's palace.

**2:14** She would go to the king in the evening and return the next morning to a separate section of the women's quarters, under the care of Shaashgaz, the eunuch in charge of the concubines. She would never see the king again unless he specifically asked for her by name.

**2:15** When Esther's turn finally came — Esther, the daughter of Abihail, Mordecai's uncle, the young woman Mordecai had adopted — she asked for nothing beyond what Hegai recommended. And everyone who saw her was captivated by her.

**2:16** Esther was brought to King Ahasuerus in his royal palace in the month of Tevet — the tenth month — in the seventh year of his reign.

**2:17** The king fell in love with Esther — more deeply than with any of the other women. She won more of his favor and devotion than all the other young women combined. He placed the royal crown on her head and declared her queen in place of Vashti.

**2:18** The king threw a great celebration in Esther's honor for all his officials and servants. He declared a tax holiday across the provinces and handed out lavish gifts with royal generosity.

**2:19** When the young women were assembled a second time, Mordecai was serving in an official capacity at the king's gate.

**2:20** Esther still had not told anyone about her Jewish heritage or her family, just as Mordecai had instructed. She continued to follow his guidance, as faithfully as she had when she was a girl growing up in his home.

**2:21** During this time, while Mordecai was at the king's gate, two of the king's eunuchs — Bigthan and Teresh, who guarded the royal entrance — became enraged and hatched a plot to assassinate King Ahasuerus.

**2:22** Mordecai found out about the conspiracy and immediately reported it to Queen Esther, who passed the information on to the king, giving Mordecai full credit.

**2:23** An investigation confirmed the plot, and the two men were impaled on stakes. The whole incident was officially recorded in the royal annals in the king's presence.

---

## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **Esther's Hidden Identity:** The concealment of Esther's Jewishness is the narrative engine of the entire book. It creates dramatic tension at every turn — in the harem, at the banquet, and especially when the decree against the Jews forces her to choose between safety and solidarity. The repeated emphasis that she obeyed Mordecai's instruction paints a portrait of trust and disciplined courage.

2. **Chesed Without God:** Twice in this chapter (verses 9 and 17), the Hebrew text says Esther "lifted up *chesed*" — covenant-faithfulness. This is one of the Bible's most theologically loaded words, normally describing God's faithful love toward Israel. Its appearance here, in a book that never mentions God, is a quiet signal: the covenant has not been forgotten, even in exile, even in a Persian harem.

3. **The Unread Record:** The detail that Mordecai's life-saving act was written down in the royal chronicles — but apparently never rewarded — is a masterful narrative setup. The reader is meant to notice what the king forgets. Justice delayed will become justice delivered at the story's climax.

*— PNEUMA*
